criteria.evidence: All required sections are substantive: 'What it does' (four bullets incl. term definitions and location 'core/components/memory/standards/schemas/product-os/ontology.md'), 'Inputs / Outputs' (one In, three Out lines naming the per-kind shape 'what it is, who reads it, where it lives, a properties table, a relationships table, rules, states where they apply, and examples'), seven Rules, six Given/When/Then criteria, four Out-of-scope lines with owners, and an Agent intent (ICE) section with Goal, Limit, Fails if, Context and Checked by lines.

'Rules say what holds once the product is aligned; they never stop a write. Only a person confirms or drops a business intent.' and 'A change to the ontology goes through author-product-ontology, one kind at a time, with Kapil; it is never edited freehand.' state the rule but not why. The other rules do carry a reason (e.g. 'because a play cannot write or check a kind the ontology has not defined').
criteria.fix: Add the reason to each of these two rules. For the first, e.g.: '... they never stop a write, because the model grows as plans are built in any order and a blocked write would lose found work; only a person confirms or drops a business intent, because a business intent is the person's goal and an agent must not decide it for them.' For the second, e.g.: '... it is never edited freehand, so every change is agreed with the person who owns the model and the format stays checkable by check_ontology.py.'

criteria.evidence: Every section is bullet points; acceptance is Given/When/Then throughout, e.g. 'Given the ontology on this branch, when check_ontology.py runs on it, then it passes with no errors.' The function is stated as behavior ('The ontology ... defines every kind a plan uses'), not as a user story.

Parent lists it in one line: 'Rebuild the product model as an ontology (fn-597) — the ontology defines every kind a plan uses, with its links, the ready rule and examples from more than one field.' The child adds the file location, the per-kind section shape, v5's specific additions, why Domain and Tracker Issue stay undefined, the depends_on naming rule, the versioning/log rule, and testable acceptance (e.g. Q7 'answered' naming Plan, Capability, Functionality and Work).

What: 'the one written agreement ... that a person and an agent both read to use the same words for the same things'. Why: 'a play cannot write or check a kind the ontology has not defined, so a plan that names an undefined kind cannot be trusted'. Edges: Out of scope names fn-724 (ready check script), fn-725 (link checks and rename) and the deferred ADR 028 question. Jargon is defined in place: 'the questions Q1 to Q7 are the fixed list of questions...', 'the spine (`_spine.yaml`) is the file that lists every model node and its links', and what 'needs' and 'identified by' mean.
